alternatives.reason_rejected: Binary, unmergeable; every merge would conflict.

alternatives.option: Keep JSON files as the runtime store
alternatives.reason_rejected: Non-atomic whole-file rewrites, O(n) per op, lockfile races — all confirmed live by the multiwriter soak.

context: Design review found the JSON-file layout unsafe under the multi-session concurrency the product exists for, and its monolithic committed files (decisions/index.json, graph/*.json) are merge-conflict magnets.
rationale: SQLite files are binary and unmergeable, so committing the db would trade one problem for another; a per-ULID export tree union-merges across branches with zero conflicts while WAL handles same-machine concurrency. Mirrors git's own object-store/index split.
summary: SQLite is the runtime store and git is the replication transport — twining.db is a gitignored derived cache, the committed truth is a per-record export tree
